title: Kimi K3.1 Pro weights are on Hugging Face. It is a 2.8-trillion-parameter model
friendlyTitle: Kimi K3.1 Pro's weights are public. It is a 2.8-trillion-parameter model
summary: Moonshot AI has put Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Hugging Face. The model card describes a mixture-of-experts model with 2.8 trillion total parameters, 104 billion active, a 1-million-token context, and text plus image input. Weights are MXFP4, activations MXFP8. Moonshot's tech blog, which said the weights would be out by 4 November, also offers Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, at two to three times the speed, on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the API. On the card, Terminal-Bench 4.0 is 65.7 at maximum effort, run with the Claude Code harness. Moonshot's table puts that ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 58.2 and just behind Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4. Those comparison numbers are the maximums Moonshot says it took from model posts or the official leaderboard, not a single shared run. The license on the card is Moonshot's own Kimi K3.1 Pro license.
friendlySummary: Moonshot AI has published the Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Hugging Face. The model card says it is a mixture-of-experts model: 2.8 trillion parameters in total, with 104 billion used for each token. The context window is 1 million tokens. It takes text and images. The weights are stored in a compressed MXFP4 format. Moonshot's tech blog, which said the weights would be out by 4 November, also offers a faster version, Kimi K3.1 Pro Highspeed, at two to three times the speed, on Kimi.ai, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and the API. On a coding-agent test called Terminal-Bench 4.0, the card lists a score of 65.7 at the highest effort setting, using Claude Code to run the tasks. Moonshot's table puts that ahead of GPT-6 Astra at 58.2 and just behind Claude Opus 5.5 at 66.4. Those other scores are the highest numbers Moonshot says it found in model posts or on the official board, not one shared test. The license is Moonshot's own Kimi K3.1 Pro license, not a standard open-source license.
whyItMatters: Do not line 65.7 up against Ripple's 80.52. Those are different tests, and this one was run through Claude Code. A 2.8-trillion-parameter model is not a download for a laptop, even in a compressed weight format. If you are going to serve it, read the license before you ship a product on the weights, and budget for a cluster, not a GPU you already own.
